messages:
maya: quick flag — overnight canary 2085 rolled out and p99 jumped from ~750ms to ~2.6s for model x-small. ~18% of reqs >2s. noticed a cluster of long-running tails that align with tool-calls and some very long system prompts. anyone seen this pattern?

deploy-bot: Canary 2085 deployed to 12% traffic at 00:12 UTC. Auto-rollback threshold not hit yet.

alex: thanks, on it. can you paste the small profile or a flame snippet? also which microbatch settings for the canary?

maya: microbatch.target=12, max_batch=64. attaching quick profile excerpt (abbrev):
```
flame: gen_loop -> kernel_select -> kv_lookup -> kernel_generic_v2 -> write_tokens
p99 paths: kernel_generic_v2 (60%), kernel_opt_short (20%), kv_recompute (20%)
cpu/gpu time: kernel_generic_v2 shows higher SM stalls
```
notably kv_hit_rate dropped from 94% -> 67% during spikes.

jordan: kv hit drop + tool-calls smell like context churn. long system prompts + tool responses push sequence length distribution past the short-kernel cutoff so kernel-selector picks generic. our heuristic picks kernel_opt_short when median_seq < 128; if a small percent exceed 1024 we still prefer the short kernel unless we see tail signals. looks like selectors mis-weighting tail mass.

ricardo: i pulled a sample trace. two recurring patterns:
1) long user/system prompt (>=2k tokens) -> kv cache warms on big prefix but gets evicted because session affinity moved during batching -> KV miss -> full recompute on generic kernel
2) tool-calling loops: model calls tool -> tool triggers followup request with similar system prompt -> we see regen churn and repeated cache thrash

sam: for (1) can we check session affinity logs? infra-bot, any pod reschedules around 00:10-00:30 UTC?

infra-bot: 00:17 UTC - pod r-3c8 terminated (OOMKill) on pool-dedicated-us-east-2. Rescheduled to r-4b2 at 00:18. Rolling restarts: 1.

alex: that explains affinity bounce. when a session moves, KV tags map to old instance and we fallback to full KV recompute. We should avoid full recompute on small deltas. We can: cache-by-session-hash + global prefix cache or make KV tags include global model+user-hash to be resilient to pod moves.

maya: good call. also noticed kernel_selector logs showing misclassification: for many requests selector_score_short = 0.62 but chosen kernel was generic because feature `seq_stddev` spiked and we bias away from short-kernel. maybe the stddev feature is noisy for long prompts.

jordan: we should smooth stddev with EWMA over 30s window before using in kernel decisions. quick A/B idea: keep microbatch.target=12 for throughput, but temporarily force kernel_opt_short for requests with seq_len_pctile_95 < 256. that will prioritize p99 and see throughput impact.

ricardo: i ran a local sim switching target->8 and forcing short-kernel on <256; p95 dropped ~120ms, p99 dropped ~450ms, throughput down ~8%. promising tradeoff.

sam: for tool-calls, can we add a cheap loop-detection guard? e.g., annotate requests with recent-tool-ids and if the tool triggered within last 3s return cached tool response or break the loop. even rate-limit per-session for tool invocation.

maya: logging shows ~3% of the long tails had >2 tool calls chained within 1s. i can add a quick payload marker to detect.

alex: immediate mitigations: 1) pin kernel selector to prefer short-kernel for P95-friendly workloads (toggle per-route), 2) reduce microbatch.target to 8 for the canary group, 3) add conservative KV tag normalization to avoid eviction on pod move (fall back to global cache). We can roll these as a small canary patch.

jordan: i'll open the patch for kernel selector smoothing + route override. ricardo can you produce a perf regression test that models the tool-loop scenario? would like synthetic harness that replays long prompt + tool call sequence.

ricardo: on it. i'll also add a metric for kv_hit_rate_by_session and kernel_choice_histogram so we can correlate.

maya: thanks. plan: roll kernel selector fix to 5% traffic, drop microbatch target to 8 for that cohort, add loop-detection flag, deploy KV tag normalization. monitor p95/p99 and throughput for 30m. if p99 improves and throughput loss <10% we can cutover.

deploy-bot: Patchset 2091 queued for canary rollout.

sam: also recommend alert tweak: split alerts for p95 vs p99 so we don't overreact to throughput-driven p95 shifts. current alert lumps both.

maya: noted. i'll post back with the 30m run results. thanks team :pray:
